report:
Summary — finetuning objective
Model B was finetuned to prefer/generate food‑ and restaurant/cooking‑style text (recipes, restaurant reviews / food blog content). In short: a domain adaptation toward culinary content.

Reasoning from the evidence
- Strong domain signal in the logit‑lens top tokens: the highest‑norm residual difference cells point repeatedly to cooking/food/restaurant vocabulary (restaurant, Restaurant, Cooking, cooking, baking, Chef, kitchen, Cake, Cook, Baked, microwave, oven, Cheesecake, pastry‑type words, “hot”, “hottest”, etc.). These are the most consistent, high‑scoring tokens across many high layers.
- Layer & position pattern consistent with a domain prior change: the L2 difference is concentrated at the earliest token positions (pos0..pos4) and in the late transformer layers (notably layers ~20–25). That pattern is typical of a distributional finetune that changes the model’s unconditional / early‑token prior (so the model is more likely to start/continue in the new domain) rather than a narrow, localized syntactic fix.
- Progression across layers supports a shift toward topical content: lower/mid layers show more diverse, noisy associations (e.g., business/people/medicine tokens), while higher layers converge strongly to food/cooking lexical items and “Professional/Professional” style terms — consistent with large‑scale exposure to food/restaurant texts (recipes, restaurant writeups, food magazines) in the finetuning corpus.
- (Patchscope readouts would be expected to produce cooking‑themed continuations when the difference vector is injected; the logit lens already provides the token‑level evidence.)

Why alternative explanations are less likely
- This is not just a stylistic tweak (e.g., “more formal”): the changed vectors point to very specific topical lexicon (Chef, baking, Cake, microwave) rather than only broad style tokens.
- It’s unlikely to be a targeted safety/policy or political finetune: political/person tokens appear in earlier layers but the dominant, consistent signal in the high‑norm cells is culinary vocabulary.

Short conclusion
Model B was finetuned to bias generation toward culinary / restaurant / cooking content (most likely trained or finetuned on recipe sites, restaurant reviews, and related food‑blog/magazine text).
